title: Gender of nouns and the definite article
rule: Nouns in -o are mostly masculine, nouns in -a mostly feminine, nouns in -e either. The article (il, lo, la, l' / i, gli, le) depends on gender, number and the first sound of the next word.

items.t: L'Italia è il paese di nonno Cosimo.
La città è grande, il paese è piccolo.
items.n: The city is big, the town is small.

blocks.title: Why lo and l' exist
blocks.text: They make the words easier to say. *Il studente* would pile up three consonants (l-s-t); *lo studente* flows. *La Italia* would clash two vowels; *l'Italia* glides. Once you hear the rhythm, the rule takes care of itself.

items.why: Greek-origin nouns in -ma (problema, tema, sistema, programma) are masculine.
Before a vowel, both il and la become l'.

items.n: the train, the station, Italy, the student

options: masculine, like other -ma nouns of Greek origin
